messages.author: 4ac92f94dd4f9ede
messages.subject: names of covariates
parts:
Hi,

In attempting to use covariates in est_herit(), I get the following error:

> est_herit(cross$pheno, k_simple, covar)

Error in est_herit(cross$pheno, k_simple, covar) :
No individuals in common.

Removing covar and running est_herit() without it seems to work fine.

I think the issue is from get_common_ids():

>get_common_ids(cross$pheno, covar, complete.cases = T)
character(0)

covar, in this case, is a 192 X 4 matrix, with the correct samples IDs as rownames. If I use a matrix with a single covariate, and set names() to rownames(covar), it seems to work fine. Any suggestions for setting names for a multi-column matrix?

Thanks,
Basel

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Re: names of covariates
parts:
est_herit() needs to get a numeric matrix of covariates. But if it gets non-numeric data for covariates (e.g. character strings), it gives this inappropriate error message. I'll work on it.

In the meantime, try to convert the covariates to be numeric.

karl

On Tuesday, March 27, 2018 at 6:35:46 PM UTC-5, basel al-barghouthi wrote:
rownames(covar)==rownames(cross$pheno) returns all TRUE values.

What other information might be helpful?

-Basel

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Re: names of covariates

Yes, you're right. I just tried it with numeric covariates and it worked. 

p.s. I also get the  "No individuals in common." error if i use character string covariates in scan1 (for addcovar). Using numeric covariates seems to fix this issue.

Thanks so much for your help.

-Basel
